drug_class: Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitor (SNRI) — a type of antidepressant
purpose: Duloxetine is used to treat depression and anxiety disorders. It is also used to relieve certain types of chronic pain, such as nerve pain from diabetes, fibromyalgia, and musculoskeletal pain. Some people take it for stress urinary incontinence as well.
how_it_works: Your brain uses natural chemicals called serotonin and norepinephrine to help regulate your mood and how you feel pain. Duloxetine works by keeping more of these chemicals available in your brain for longer. This helps improve your mood, reduce anxiety, and lessen the sensation of pain throughout your body.
common_side_effects: Nausea (especially when you first start), dry mouth, feeling sleepy or tired, dizziness, constipation, sweating more than usual, decreased appetite, and trouble sleeping. Most of these tend to improve after the first couple of weeks.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly — always talk to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly can cause withdrawal symptoms like dizziness, irritability, or flu-like feelings. This medication can raise blood pressure, so your doctor may monitor it. It may increase thoughts of self-harm in some young people, especially at the start of treatment — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as serious interactions are possible.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 30 mg once a day, often taken in the morning with or without food. Your doctor may increase this to 60 mg once daily after one to two weeks. Some conditions may require up to 120 mg per day, split into doses. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed and swallow the capsule whole — do not crush or chew it.
